subject: Terra Ops - dedicated fleet scenario planning & fallback lanes
messages:
From: Claire Tan <claire@terra.ai>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@terra.ai, ops@terra.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fleet sizing scenarios for Terra deployment

Hi Rafael / Redwood team,

We're kicking off sizing for the Terra generative product deployment and want Redwood's recommendations on dedicated fleet sizing across regions. High level:
- Expected steady state QPS: 120 qps (text-gen few-shot LLM, 2-3s latency target)
- Peak concurrency (burst): ~450 concurrent requests for short spikes tied to morning batch windows
- Models: an optimized open Llama-X variant (quantized) for production and a larger backbone for higher-quality requests during business hours
- Target regions: primary in APAC (Singapore/HK), fallback in EU (Ireland), secondary US (Oregon)

Ask: can you provide 3 scenarios (conservative / typical / aggressive) with: per-region GPU counts (A100-80GB equiv), burst buffer strategy, estimated lead time to provision new APAC cluster, and a short note on availability risks? We'll need cost ballpark and a draft SOW for procurement.

Would like to review internally by next Wednesday — can you confirm a short deck or spreadsheet by EOD Wednesday (10/7)? Also open to a 30m sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Claire Tan
VP Ops, Terra AI

---
Attachments: none

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
To: Claire Tan <claire@terra.ai>, ops@terra.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, procurement@terra.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fleet sizing scenarios for Terra deployment

Claire — thanks for the clear brief. I've attached a demand model (terra_demand_model_v3.xlsx) and an initial SOW draft (sow_draft_terra.pdf) that map the scenarios you requested. High-level summary below; the sheet contains the modeled token/time/QPS assumptions and cost math.

Quick summary (very short):
- Conservative: APAC 24 x A100-80GB equiv (sustained), EU 12, US 8. Burst buffer = shared routed burst (20%) via dedicated reserved burst lanes.
- Typical: APAC 48, EU 24, US 16; 25% burst lanes + prefix cache to reduce token cost.
- Aggressive: APAC 80, EU 40, US 24; includes reserved startup nodes for 2-week ramp; suggests dedicated warm pool in APAC.

Lead time: we can provision an APAC private pool (Singapore region) in ~6 weeks for basic capacity, 10+ weeks for fully redundant multi-AZ setup depending on vendor supply windows.

Availability risks: GPU sourcing window (OEM deliveries), quoted SLOs may require geo-redundant standby to meet 99.95% during rolling maint. We'll call out fallback lanes (model-quantized variants + EU failover) in the SOW.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm target SLO (p50/p95 latency requirements) and acceptable fallback model for degraded mode?
2) If procurement is ready, I'll hand over the SOW and a one-pager for budgeting.

Proposing a 30m sync tomorrow 09:00 PT / 13:00 ET — does that work?

Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Attachments: terra_demand_model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), sow_draft_terra.pdf (draft SOW)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Fleet sizing scenarios for Terra deployment -- internal notes

Internal notes / suggested positions before the call:

- Pricing lanes: recommend we price the Typical scenario as our go-to sell; Conservative used for procurement comfort, Aggressive as a priced upgrade.
- SLO ask: push for p95 <= 450ms for quantized model in APAC; if customer requires lower, that will materially increase GPUs (and cost).
- Capacity asks: call out minimum reservation commitment (3-6 months) for Dedicated pool to secure GPU allocation.
- Lead time: call out a 6-10 week dependency window and include a clause for delivery timeline remedies (credits) only when Redwood controls procurement.

Operational levers to include in the SOW:
- Autoscaling policy definition (burst to reserved burst lanes).
- Warm pool sizing and pre-warming windows for daily morning spikes.
- Fallback routing: quantized smaller model + EU failover with prefix caching to reduce cold start costs.

I'll be on the call and can own commercial framing. Rafael, capture a conservative/typical/aggressive number of A100-equivalents per region in the sheet before the sync.

Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Note: internal only

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, Claire Tan <claire@terra.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Terra Ops - dedicated fleet scenario planning & fallback lanes

Claire / team — adding the technical sizing breakdown (summarized; full math in the attached sheet).

Assumptions used: average tokens per request ~650, average generation latency budget 2.5s, model memory/kv/cache overhead for Llama-X quantized path. We converted to A100-80GB equivalent using our internal kernel profile.

Sizing (A100-80GB equiv) by scenario:
- Conservative: APAC 24 (sustained), EU 12, US 8. Burst lanes: +20% capacity auto-route.
- Typical: APAC 48, EU 24, US 16. Reserved warm pool in APAC = 12 nodes.
- Aggressive: APAC 88, EU 40, US 24. Aggressive includes a 2-week safety buffer of hot nodes during ramp.

Notes & constraints:
- APAC (Singapore) region provisioning: 6 weeks for initial cluster (single AZ), 10+ weeks for multi-AZ with redundant networking. Lead time driven by rack/GPU delivery and on-ramp customs.
- If Terra requires a hard p95 SLA under 300ms, we'd need to move to higher-cost instance types (or more nodes) due to network tail latencies in APAC.
- Suggested fallback policy: during overload, route 40% of requests to quantized smaller model, 60% retain full model for enterprise customers (tagged). This preserves perceived quality while controlling spend.

Operational items for SOW edit: add explicit <ramp dates> per tranche, acceptance test steps for APAC cluster, and force-majeure/ procurement-delivery clauses. I'll update the sheet and drop the link below.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1TerraDemandModelV3

From: Claire Tan <claire@terra.ai>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, procurement@terra.ai
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Terra Ops - dedicated fleet scenario planning & fallback lanes

Thanks Rafael / Karthik / Laura — this is helpful. Procurement confirms we can accept a staged ramp and a 6-week pilot in APAC as long as the SOW includes clear acceptance criteria and a pilot rollback plan. A few quick clarifications:

- Can Redwood commit to the 6-week initial provisioning milestone for the Typical scenario if we sign the SOW by Oct 12?
- For the Aggressive scenario, we need explicit dates for when extra nodes will be available (we can't accept open-ended "10+ weeks").
- Please add a short paragraph in the SOW that describes the fallback model behavior during overload (we need deterministic routing rules for compliance).

We can take the SOW to our legal / procurement once those items are explicit. If you can update and send the revised SOW + the cost workbook by EOD Friday 10/9, procurement will start review. Otherwise let's schedule a 30m to finalize.

Claire Tan
VP Ops, Terra AI
